messages:
elaine: quick brain dump — i think the continuous-batcher is getting hard to reason about. proposal: split it into two explicit components: ingress (enqueue + cheap shape hints) and packer (windowing + build_batch). want to discuss API boundaries and tradeoffs.

sam: sounds promising. what invariants do you want between them? fairness, backpressure, kv-cache pinning?

elaine: exactly. high-level invariants i'm aiming for: 1) enqueue is non-blocking (best-effort) with headroom accounting; 2) packer owns exact batch formation and preemption; 3) minimal cross-component state — only small shape hints and deadline tags flow.

kai: curious about "non-blocking enqueue" — won't that blow up memory if packer is slow? how do we signal backpressure?

elaine: enqueue returns a light-weight token and a boolean whether request was accepted. if rejected, caller falls back to lower-tier model. acceptance uses a cheap reservation ledger (per-tenant credits). we keep queue entries compact (pointer + hint) so memory growth is bounded.

tariq: +1 but we need a transport for ownership transfer when packer wants to compact/evict. maybe lightweight lease tokens with expiry. also need to ensure kv-cache pinning doesn't leak if a request is dropped.

sam: i worry about adding another surface: packer must know enough to decide preemption without full request decode. so shape_hints must include worst-case token estimate and deadline. ops-wise, can we reuse existing admission credits ledger?

elaine: yes reuse ledger. sketch of interface:

```
// ingress
Enqueue(req_id, tenant_id, shape_hint, deadline_hint) -> (accepted:bool, token)
Cancel(token)

// packer
ClaimBatch(max_tokens) -> [token]
ReleaseTokens([token])
```

we keep token small (64b) and opaque. packer can ask for a lease extension when it actually needs to pin kv cache.

joe: how does this affect routing across GPUs? currently continuous-batcher assumes single queue per GPU. if we split, are we moving to global ingress + per-GPU packer? that adds network hops.

elaine: thinking of hierarchical mapping: ingress shards by tenant/region -> small routing table -> packer located on candidate GPUs. ingress only forwards a pointer to the packer (not the full input). we avoid heavy copies.

kai: still worried about headroom oscillation. packer should expose a quick "expected_fill_rate" metric so ingress can adapt reservation aggressiveness.

tariq: also need graceful fallback for long-tailed requests: if packer keeps extending lease repeatedly we should have a circuit breaker that forces eviction to keep SLO for short requests.

sam: operational concerns: telemetry must tie token -> request metadata for postmortem. also we should be able to debug lost tokens. add a debug trace id into token payload.

elaine: rollout plan: implement ingress + local packer in-process first (no cross-node routing). fold in ledger and metrics, run canary on one pool, measure tail latency and memory. if good, enable remote packer routing.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: batcher-refactor/ingress-pack - canary -> infra-stage at 12:30 UTC

joe: one small nit: we should model the enforcement policy as "soft accept + reclaimable reservation" rather than hard accept/reject. that gives better PLG UX (less 503s).

elaine: agree. make acceptance best-effort with reclaim policy. packer can preempt reclaimable reservations under overload and emit metric `reservation.reclaimed`.

sam: ok — next steps: small spike to implement token format + ledger reuse, then design preemption circuit breaker. i'll take spike.

elaine: thanks — i'll write a short RFC with the interface sketch and telemetry checklist. ping me if you want pair on ledger reuse. :thumbsup:

kai: +1. would like to run sims for headroom oscillation once spike exists.

joe: ack

elaine: closing thread — moving details to RFC draft in docs/ rfc link will follow.
